setupSteps: Clear the space. About 1.5 m wide x 1.2 m deep (est.). Move rugs that slide, shoes, and anything the feet could catch. Check overhead: ceiling fans, low lights and loft beds.

Floor and noise: a non-slip floor. In a flat with neighbours below, do the step jack only, on a yoga mat or thick carpet, and keep the foot landing soft. Avoid early morning and late night with the jump version.
Footwear: flat, supportive trainers for the jump version; barefoot or trainers for step jacks. Avoid socks on smooth tiles (slipping).
Starting stance: stand tall, feet together or just hip-width apart, toes pointing forward, arms by your sides (Pfizer; WebMD).
Posture: chest lifted, shoulders relaxed and down, stomach lightly braced, eyes looking forward at a fixed spot.
Hands: open and relaxed, palms facing inwards or forwards, arms nearly straight but elbows not locked hard.
Clothing: fitted top and track pants or leggings so the camera can see shoulders and knees; a supportive sports bra if needed for comfort.
Water and fan: keep water nearby; use a fan, because this move warms up quickly.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Stand tall and brace
steps.action: Feet together or hip-width, arms by your sides, gently tighten your stomach.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ear, shoulder, hip and ankle roughly in one line. Front: feet together, shoulders level.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Shift weight to the left foot
steps.action: Let your weight rest on the left foot, with a soft knee.
steps.feel: Left foot and hip take the weight.
steps.visualCheck: Front: hips stay level, not swaying.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Step the right foot out to the side
steps.action: Take a comfortable step out to the right (about shoulder-width plus a little, est.), landing softly on the ball of the foot then lowering the heel; toes point forward or slightly out.
steps.feel: Gentle push in the outer hips.
steps.visualCheck: Front: right foot clearly wider than the shoulders' width apart; knee over the second toe.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Raise both arms overhead as the foot goes out
steps.action: Sweep both arms out to the sides and up, until the hands are overhead or as high as is comfortable (palms may touch).
steps.feel: Shoulders lifting, chest open; no pinching at the shoulder tip.
steps.visualCheck: Front: arms form a "Y"; shoulders stay down, not shrugged to the ears.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Step the right foot back in
steps.action: Bring the right foot back to meet the left, landing softly.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Lower the arms
steps.action: Bring the arms down in a controlled sweep to your sides, in time with step 5.
steps.visualCheck: Front: hands back by the thighs, not slapping them.

steps.part: A. Low-impact step jack (beginner main version)
steps.title: Repeat on the left
steps.action: Step the left foot out and raise the arms again, then return. Alternate sides.
steps.breathing: Out as you step out, in as you step back (est.; any steady pattern is fine, never hold your breath).
steps.visualCheck: Front: left and right steps look the same width.

steps.title: Stand tall, feet together, arms at sides
Jump both feet out to slightly wider than shoulder width while the arms sweep overhead (NASM; Pfizer)
Land softly on the balls of the feet with soft knees; the heels touch down lightly
Jump the feet back together while the arms come down
Keep a steady rhythm of about 1 rep per second (est.), staying light on the feet

commonMistakes.title: Locking the knees on landing
commonMistakes.text: Locking the knees on landing. Why: the shock goes straight up the knees and spine (NASM names landing with straight knees as a common error). Fix: keep a small knee bend and land on the balls of the feet, then lower the heels.

commonMistakes.title: Landing flat and loud
commonMistakes.text: Landing flat and loud. Why: harder landings mean higher joint load and noise through the floor. Fix: step out (low-impact version) or land on the toes and roll down quietly; slow the rhythm.

commonMistakes.title: Knees caving in or toes turning far out
commonMistakes.text: Knees caving in or toes turning far out. Why: twists the knee and strains the ankle. Fix: point the knees over the second toe; make the step narrower.

commonMistakes.title: Arms stopping at shoulder height or flapping unevenly
commonMistakes.text: Arms stopping at shoulder height or flapping unevenly. Why: less work and an uneven rhythm. Fix: reach both arms up together to overhead (or as high as is pain-free) and bring them down together.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging the shoulders and arching the lower back as the arms go up
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging the shoulders and arching the lower back as the arms go up. Why: pinches the neck and loads the lower back. Fix: ribs down, stomach lightly in, shoulders away from the ears; use arms to shoulder height if overhead pinches.

commonMistakes.title: Going too fast too soon
commonMistakes.text: Going too fast too soon. Why: form breaks down and you get dizzy or breathless. Fix: start at about 1 rep per 2 seconds with step jacks and increase speed only when breathing stays comfortable (talk test).

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: breath-holding raises blood pressure more than breathing during effort. Fix: breathe out as the arms go up (or any steady pattern) and keep talking-pace breathing.

commonMistakes.title: Doing it on slippery or hard floors in socks
commonMistakes.text: Doing it on slippery or hard floors in socks. Why: slips and joint jolts. Fix: non-slip floor, mat or shoes.

safetyNotes: Knee, ankle or hip problems (arthritis, injury, replacements): do step jacks only, or arms-only jacks; avoid the jump version if it hurts. Pfizer advises knee or ankle pain and osteoarthritis users to check with a healthcare provider.

Osteoporosis: low-level impact is recommended for bone strength in general osteoporosis advice, but people with vertebral or multiple fractures should stay at brisk-walking-level impact and get individual advice (Strong, Steady and Straight).
Back problems: step jacks with a braced stomach; avoid arching as the arms rise.
Shoulder problems: keep the arms below the painful range; use shoulder-height arms or hands on hips.
High blood pressure and heart disease: moderate effort, steady breathing, cool down gradually; get medical clearance if BP is severe or uncontrolled or you have known heart disease.
Pregnancy: balance changes raise fall risk; low-impact aerobics is listed as safe to continue in an uncomplicated pregnancy; skip the jump version and ask your obstetrician.

Postpartum and pelvic-floor symptoms: NHS trust leaflets advise avoiding jumping for at least 3 months after birth (time ranges from 12 weeks to 6–12 months across leaflets); leaking or heaviness is a signal to stop and see a women's health physiotherapist.
Recent surgery, dizziness, balance problems: only with approval; hold a wall for balance.

swapsByAccess.none: March in place with arm raises, arms-only jacks, or Surya Namaskar (Yoga & Stretch 2)
swapsByAccess.home_equipment: Step-ups on a low stair with arm raises (Home 12), or skipping rope (Home 14) if joints and noise allow
swapsByAccess.basic_gym: Treadmill brisk walk (Gym 5) or stationary bike (Gym 7)
swapsByAccess.full_gym: Elliptical (Gym 6), rowing machine (Gym 8) or stair climber (Gym 9) for low-impact cardio

conditionCautions.change: Step jacks at moderate effort (5-6/10, Borg 12-13); keep breathing; extend the cool-down; severe or uncontrolled BP needs a medical check first
Counts toward aerobic activity; usual glucose checks and fast carbohydrate on hand if on insulin or sulfonylureas; wear shoes and check feet if neuropathy
conditionCautions.source: ADA position statement (Colberg et al. 2016); ACSM 2022 consensus (via search summary)

conditionCautions.change: After clearance only: slow step jacks at light effort (3-4/10, Borg 9-11), short bouts; stop with chest discomfort or breathlessness
conditionCautions.source: AHA physical activity recommendations; clearance specifics Not found

conditionCautions.change: Counts toward 150+ minutes/week of aerobic activity alongside resistance work
conditionCautions.source: AHA recommendations; AHA statement (Gibbs et al.)

conditionCautions.change: Use the low-impact step jack; start with 3 x 30 s and build up; avoid the jump version until strength and tolerance improve
conditionCautions.source: JMU low-impact guidance; ACE obesity training article; ACSM weight management position stand (Donnelly 2009)

conditionCautions.change: Fits aerobic activity guidance; no jumping-jack-specific advice found
Train normally if controlled; start at beginner level with ongoing fatigue
Warm up 10-15 minutes before harder work, keep reliever inhaler nearby, avoid cold dry air; stop and use reliever if symptoms start
conditionCautions.source: Asthma UK tips via Pharmacy Magazine CPD; Cambridge University Hospitals leaflet; PubMed 21811185

conditionCautions.change: Step jacks or arms-only jacks only; avoid the jump version; mat and flat trainers; stop if pain rises
conditionCautions.source: Harvard Health 217-trial analysis (low-impact aerobic best for knee OA); Arthritis Foundation via Today's Dietitian; Pfizer Health Answers

conditionCautions.change: Brace stomach, ribs down, step jacks; avoid the jump version in a flare; staying active beats bed rest
conditionCautions.source: NHS hospital leaflets (Oxford University Hospitals; Sheffield); Surrey Physio (high-impact claim lower evidence)

conditionCautions.change: Raise arms only as high as comfortable (pain up to 4/10 in physio programmes; avoid painful overhead reaching when irritated); shoulder-height arms or hands on hips
conditionCautions.source: HSS shoulder impingement protocol; Pure Physiotherapy programmes

conditionCautions.change: Brief low-level impact can help bones; with vertebral or multiple fractures stay at brisk-walking-level impact (step jacks) and avoid spinal flexion; get individual advice
conditionCautions.source: Strong, Steady and Straight (Royal Osteoporosis Society, BJSM 2022); Society for Endocrinology summary

conditionCautions.change: Low-impact step jacks only in an uncomplicated pregnancy; no jumping (balance and fall risk); stop with dizziness, pain or leaking; ask obstetrician
conditionCautions.source: ACOG opinion via DONA summary; NCBI Bookshelf NBK582697 (jumping not mentioned directly)

conditionCautions.change: No jumping for at least 3 months and until cleared (leaflets range from 12 weeks to 6-12 months); step jacks only if no leaking, heaviness or pain; see a women's health physiotherapist if leaking
conditionCautions.source: Aneurin Bevan UHB physiotherapy leaflet; Oxford University Hospitals; Walsall Healthcare; West Hertfordshire leaflet

conditionCautions.change: Only with surgeon or physiotherapist approval
